findings.claim: The unsubscribe endpoint is a GET route whose action changes and saves TopicUser.notification_level without CSRF protection or a signed token, so a third-party page (e.g. via ) can change a logged-in user's notification level for any topic they can see.

verifier.reason: config/routes.rb adds `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` (and `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`) pointing to TopicsController#unsubscribe, which changes and saves `tu.notification_level` with `tu.save!` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-113) and checks no token. The `protect_from_forgery` call in app/controllers/application_controller.rb:21 does not check GET requests, so a cross-site request that carries the session cookie will change the level; TopicView.new only limits this to topics the user can see.

findings.claim: Because the unsubscribe endpoint is a GET, email client link prefetchers can trigger it and change users' notification settings without the user acting.

verifier.reason: The patch adds GET routes for unsubscribe (config/routes.rb:444-445), and TopicsController#unsubscribe saves a lower notification level on every request (topics_controller.rb, new unsubscribe action) with no confirmation step or CSRF token. A fetch that carries the user's session can change the setting without the user acting, and repeat fetches lower it further. The impact is limited because the action requires login (topics_controller.rb:8-28), so a link scanner without the session cookie only hits the login check.

findings.claim: The unsubscribe action requires ensure_logged_in, but its URL is sent in notification emails. A logged-out recipient who clicks the link is redirected to / with no message and no return path, and nothing is unsubscribed.

verifier.reason: topics_controller.rb puts :unsubscribe under the ensure_logged_in filter (patch L183-184), and application_controller.rb:97-104 handles a logged-out HTML GET with a plain redirect_to path("/"), so the TopicUser update never runs. A destination_url cookie is set at application_controller.rb:420, but login.js.es6:84 only uses it on login-required sites, so on normal sites the user lands on / after logging in.

findings.claim: The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled; it should be stopNotificationsText.

verifier.reason: The property is spelled stopNotificiationsText (with an extra 'i') at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5. The template at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 uses the same spelling, so the binding still works and this is only a naming typo.

findings.claim: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, TopicUser.find_by can return nil when the user has no topic_users row for the topic. The next line calls tu.notification_level without a nil check, which raises and returns a 500.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb, the new unsubscribe action calls `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` (patch line 204) and then calls `tu.notification_level` (line 206) without a nil check. TopicView.new does not create a topic_users row (lib/topic_view.rb never references TopicUser), so a logged-in user with no row for that topic, such as one following an email link for a topic they never opened, gets a NoMethodError and a 500.

findings.claim: The unsubscribe action steps the notification level down instead of setting a target level, so it is not idempotent. Watching/tracking goes to regular on the first visit and to muted on a reload or prefetch.

verifier.reason: In TopicsController#unsubscribe (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb, patch lines 206-212), the level depends on the current value: anything above regular is set to regular, otherwise it is set to muted, and the result is saved on every GET. Opening the link once takes watching/tracking to regular, and any later GET (a reload, prefetch or link scanner) takes it to muted.

findings.claim: After a watching/tracking user's first click, the confirmation says 'You will stop receiving notifications', but the level was only lowered to regular, which still notifies on replies, mentions and quotes.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb (unsubscribe), a level above regular, meaning watching or tracking, is only lowered to regular; muting happens only on a later visit. Yet the page always shows 'You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}' (config/locales/client.en.yml stop_notifications, rendered by templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs), and at the regular level Discourse still notifies on replies, mentions and quotes.

findings.claim: The test for the List-Unsubscribe header only checks that the header is present, not that its value uses the provided unsubscribe_url.

verifier.reason: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:174-175 only asserts that `header_args['List-Unsubscribe']` is `be_present`, even though the patch now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`. The weak check hides that lib/email/message_builder.rb:107 still builds the header from `template_args[:user_preferences_url]` and ignores unsubscribe_url.

findings.claim: The List-Unsubscribe header still points to the user preferences page rather than the per-topic unsubscribe URL.

verifier.reason: lib/email/message_builder.rb:107 still sets List-Unsubscribe to template_args[:user_preferences_url]. The unsubscribe_url the patch passes in (user_notifications.rb:295, and the List-Unsubscribe header spec at message_builder_spec.rb) only reaches the body text, not this header.

findings.claim: On line 10, the header's class attribute contains '.previous-discussion' with a leading dot, which prevents CSS from targeting it.

verifier.reason: app/views/email/notification.html.erb:10 has `class='.previous-discussion'`, so the element's class is literally `.previous-discussion`. The `.previous-discussion` selector in lib/email/styles.rb:75 looks for the class `previous-discussion` without the dot, so the inline style is never applied. The same typo is on the removed line, so the patch only re-indented existing code.

findings.claim: Adding render :show inside perform_show_response renders the template before topics#show sets canonical_url, so server-rendered topic pages lose their <link rel="canonical"> tag.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `render :show` inside `format.html` in `perform_show_response` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb ~line 500). With Rails 4.1.10 that renders the page straight away, before `show` sets `canonical_url` at topics_controller.rb:87, so `canonical_link_tag` in app/views/layouts/_head.html.erb:9 finds `@canonical_url` nil and outputs '' (lib/canonical_url.rb:15). Before the patch the page was rendered automatically after the action finished, so the URL was already set.

findings.claim: The view exists only to add a CSS class that the template's wrapper div could carry directly.

verifier.reason: views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:1-3 only sets `classNames: ["topic-unsubscribe"]`. The template's wrapper `<div class="container">` in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:1 could carry `topic-unsubscribe` directly, and the descendant selectors in topic.scss:166-176 would still match.

findings.claim: About 100 of the 225 changed lines are formatting-only edits unrelated to the feature, contrary to CONTRIBUTING.md's one-feature-per-branch guidance.

verifier.reason: The patch changes about 225 lines, and roughly 100–120 of them only reformat code the feature doesn't need: topic-from-params.js.es6 (var→const and method shorthand), topic_user.rb (scope, create_lookup and MessageBus.publish calls), the whole of notification.html.erb, message_builder.rb:458-499, user_notifications.rb's from_alias line and a route reorder. CONTRIBUTING.md:40 asks for 'one feature or bug-fix per branch'.

findings.claim: On the unsubscribe page, {{title}} is interpolated into an HTML translation and inserted with triple-stash without escaping, which allows XSS.

verifier.reason: The template uses triple-stash for stopNotificiationsText (templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:139), which fills in model.fancyTitle (controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:29). That value is already HTML-escaped on the server, because Topic#fancy_title calls ERB::Util.html_escape(title) (app/models/topic.rb:264), so user-controlled markup cannot get through.

findings.claim: The slug-mismatch redirect for the unsubscribe URL, which has side effects, uses status 301, so browsers cache it permanently.

verifier.reason: The patch's new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (patch line 201, app/controllers/topics_controller.rb ~line 102) does `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301` when the slug doesn't match. The GET action then changes state by lowering the TopicUser notification level and calling `tu.save!`. The practical harm is small: the cached 301 points to the canonical unsubscribe URL, which still runs the action, and this copies the 301 that the existing `show` action already uses.

findings.claim: The template is at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which resolves to a nested topic.unsubscribe route. The router, controller and view use the top-level topicUnsubscribe route, so Ember will not pick up the template.

verifier.reason: Discourse's custom resolver finds this template. In findTemplate (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/ember/resolver.js.es6:151,158), the route name 'topicUnsubscribe' is decamelized to 'topic_unsubscribe', and the first '_' is replaced with '/', giving 'topic/unsubscribe'. That is the template added at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, so it is picked up for the top-level route.

findings.claim: The post_number: /\d+/ constraint was dropped from both summary routes, and moderator-liked was reordered, inside a feature commit.

verifier.reason: In config/routes.rb (patch lines 438-446), the patch removes `post_number: /\d+/` from both summary routes, leaving only `{topic_id: /\d+/}`. It also moves the moderator-liked route below `t/:topic_id/wordpress`. Neither change has anything to do with the unsubscribe feature the patch adds. The routes have no :post_number segment, so the removed constraint probably did nothing anyway.

findings.claim: The multiline array passed to skip_before_filter has no trailing comma after :unsubscribe.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb (patch lines 188-189) the skip_before_filter array is the single-line `only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`, not a multiline array. The multiline array that ends in `:unsubscribe]` belongs to the earlier `before_filter ... except:` list (patch lines 180-184), and leaving out a trailing comma there is valid Ruby that matches the original code's style.

findings.claim: There are no tests for the new state-changing TopicsController#unsubscribe endpoint, Topic#unsubscribe_url, or the email footer change, contrary to CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Include tests' guidance.

verifier.reason: The only spec change is spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172. It passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` so the new interpolation key resolves, but it asserts nothing about the link. No spec mentions TopicsController#unsubscribe (topics_controller.rb:197-215) or Topic#unsubscribe_url (topic.rb:719), even though CONTRIBUTING.md:44 says to include tests.

findings.claim: TopicsController#unsubscribe calls tu.save! directly instead of TopicUser.change. As a result, notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at are not set and the MessageBus notification_level_change publish is skipped, so update_last_read auto-tracking can later overwrite the user's choice.

verifier.reason: The new TopicsController#unsubscribe (patch lines 204-212) sets tu.notification_level and calls tu.save!, so it skips TopicUser.change, which is the code that sets notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id and publishes notification_level_change (app/models/topic_user.rb:87-90, 112-114); TopicUser has no save callbacks that would set them. Because notifications_reason_id stays null, the CASE in update_last_read (topic_user.rb:160-164) can switch the user back to tracking on a later read, overriding the unsubscribe.

findings.claim: The shared unsubscribe_link i18n string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but Email::MessageBuilder gives it no default. Any build_email caller passing add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url hits a missing-interpolation error, and non-English locales keep the old string.

verifier.reason: The only caller that passes add_unsubscribe_link: true is app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:294, and the patch now passes unsubscribe_url there (line 295); RejectionMailer blocks that option and no plugins use it, so nothing hits the missing-interpolation error. Non-English locales do keep the old string, which only drops the new link and causes no error.

findings.claim: An in-app Ember transition to topicUnsubscribe only loads the topic JSON and never calls the server action, yet still shows the 'stop receiving notifications' confirmation.

verifier.reason: The new route's model hook (routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:111-117) calls only PostStream.loadTopicView, which fetches /t/<id>.json (post-stream.js.es6:811-823) and never reaches topics#unsubscribe. The template still renders the 'You will stop receiving notifications' text (templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:139), so an in-app transition shows the confirmation without changing the notification level. Following the email link is a full page load that does run the server action.

findings.claim: On line 6, the email template repeats the respond instructions that already appear on line 19 when context_posts are present.

verifier.reason: In app/views/email/notification.html.erb, line 6 (inside `if context_posts.present?`) and line 19 both output `%{respond_instructions}`, and the `gsub!` in lib/email/message_builder.rb:494 fills in both, so the instructions show twice when there are context posts. The patch only re-indented this: the old template already had the same two placeholders, and the repeat looks deliberate, once after the main post and once at the bottom.

findings.claim: The controller exists only to format one i18n string, which the i18n helper with named params could do directly in the template.

verifier.reason: The new controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 (patch lines 26-31) only defines `stopNotificiationsText`, which calls I18n.t with `{title: model.fancyTitle}`. The `i18n` helper in helpers/i18n.js.es6:3-4 already passes hash params through to I18n.t, and templates already use it this way (e.g. templates/topic.hbs:94 `{{{i18n "queue.has_pending_posts" count=...}}}`), so `{{{i18n "topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications" title=model.fancyTitle}}}` would do the same job.

findings.claim: The rewritten tracking scope uses 3-space and 5-space continuation indents, unlike the file's 2-space convention.

verifier.reason: In app/models/topic_user.rb:10-12 the patch moves `.where(` to column 3 (3 spaces), which is less indented than `where(topic_id: topic_id)` at line 9 (4 spaces). Its arguments sit at 5 spaces. Every other line in the file is indented in steps of 2 spaces.

findings.claim: The module ends in }) without a semicolon, unlike its sibling .js.es6 controllers.

verifier.reason: The new file app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:9 ends in `})` with no semicolon. A search of the controllers directory finds no other controller ending in a bare `})`, so this file breaks the pattern of its siblings.
